newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks dip on small-investor profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks dip on small-investor profit-taking.

text.p: Peruvian shares declined Monday as small local investors took advantage of last week's gains to take profits, but trade was thin due to the Presidents' Day holiday in the United States, brokers said.
"We hope the return of foreign investors bolster confidence among locals to strongly enter the market," said Hernando Pastor of T & J brokerage.
The General Index dipped 0.52 percent to 1,540.45 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index slipped 0.66 percent to 2,217.89 points.
In a total of 1,141 trades, volume was estimated at 23.4 million soles ($8.9 million) as 29 stocks fell, 29 were stable and 14 advanced.

Biggest losers included brewery Compania Nacional de Cerveza, off 2.26 percent to 1.30 soles and another brewery Backus y Johnston, which dipped 0.89 percent to 2.22 soles. Benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed level at 5.83 soles.
